newsitem.title: FINLAND: WEEK AHEAD - FINNISH CORPORATE EARNINGS IN FOCUS.
newsitem.headline: WEEK AHEAD - FINNISH CORPORATE EARNINGS IN FOCUS.

text.p: Outlook for Finnish financial markets next week according to analysts:
* Stock market operators will focus on full-year corporate earnings reports,
* Strong dollar will continue to support the markka, with DEM/FIM seen trading in a 2.91-2.96 range,
* Mixed views on what German Bundesbank's will do with key rates at its regular council meeting on Thursday,
* Finnish tender rate cut hopes seen mounting if Buba decides to ease its repo rate
DOMESTIC COMPANY EARNINGS IN FOCUS
With several large companies reporting 1996 earnings the the home market will remain in focus, equities analysts said.
"Investors will be digesting earnings reports of the big companies," said Roar Nilsen, chief analyst at Carnegie Securities in Helsinki.

Enskilda Securities analyst Johannes Schulman said the dollar's movements will also be eyed closely as further gains in the U.S. unit could dampen the competive edge of U.S. forest and metal industry firms.
Companies reporting full-year 1996 earnings next week include Kemira, Instrumentarium, Metra, Partek, Orion, Tamro, Tampella and Alandsbanken.
STRONG DOLLAR SEEN SUPPORTING MARKKA
Dollar strength against the German mark is seen supporting the markka next week, too, analysts said.
Henrik Soerensen, analyst at Unibank Markets in Copenhagen, plotted DEM/FIM in a 2.91 to 2.96 range next week.
Besides the firmer dollar, gains in the Swedish crown are also expected to push the markka firmer against the mark, he noted.
Merita Bank chief analyst Jukka Lepomaki saw DEM/FIM drifting around 2.95. "But if the dollar/mark breaks through the 1.70 level, the DEM/FIM is likely to fall close to 2.90," he said.
TENDER RATE CUT HOPES SEEN MOUNTING IF BUBA CUTS
Some market operators expect the Bundesbank to keep its repo rate on hold at 3.00 percent while others see a 20 basis point easing at the regular council meeting on Thursday.
Finnish tender rate cut expectations will immediately mount on any German rate easing, analysts said.
FINNISH DECEMBER INDUSTRIAL OUTPUT AND JANUARY PPI
Statistics Finland (SF) will publish December industrial output on Monday at around 0700/0500 GMT and January producer price index is due at the same time on Tuesday.
December industrial production is seen growing 6.9 percent, according to a forecasts by six economists.
Domestic economic data are largely expected to be ignored by the bond and forex markets, analysts said.
U.S. January CPI figures are due on Wednesday at 1530/1330 GMT.
The State Treasury Office (STO) will hold its regular weekly T-bill auction on Tuesday. The maturities to be auctioned are 84-day, 176-day and 358-day T-bills.
